ALWAYS_L3.//: Locked categories that are always L3, whatever review.yaml's levels list (self-modification and harness-config).

ENGINE_ROOT_FILES.//: The engine's own files at the top of its repo, glob for glob (#858): like ENGINE_TREE, their locks hold only in the engine's repo. Matched exactly.

ENGINE_TREE.//: The engine's own source tree: a self-modification glob under it names an engine file, not a managed app's (its lock stands aside in a managed app's repo).

HARNESS_CONFIG_GLOBS.//: The harness's config in a repo (#798): the config folder, Claude Code's project settings and CLAUDE.md. Locked: always L3 and never auto-merged; a repo may only add to them.

LOCKED_CATEGORIES.//: The locked categories: every glob of SELF_MODIFICATION_PARTS under self-modification, HARNESS_CONFIG_GLOBS under harness-config, and the agents' instructions. Written out (#941); test/check-tables-sync.test.ts holds the first two equal to their sources.

ODD_PATH_CATEGORIES.//: The categories of a path nothing should have to read around (src/review.ts): always L3, always waits, never loosened. Each is one of review.ts's constants (CONTROL_CHARACTER_PATH, NON_UTF8_PATH, INVISIBLE_CHARACTER_PATH, NON_ASCII_TOP_LEVEL_PATH, CONFUSABLE_PATH); test/check-tables-sync.test.ts holds them equal.

SELF_MODIFICATION_PARTS.//: The harness changing its own controls (src/review.ts SELF_MODIFICATION): each part says, in the words Waiting on you shows, what a change to its globs changes; the first part a file matches names it. Each glob is in one part only. Written out from what src/review.ts built (#941): test/check-tables-sync.test.ts holds the tool guard's part to every HOOK_IMPORTS entry and the decision records' part to DECISION_RECORD_GLOBS.

deploy/**: the engine's deployment manifests (a compose file and the like) set its isolation and exposure, as the setup scripts do: the user it runs as, what it mounts, which ports it publishes. Locked before the first one exists.

The engine's container image (Dockerfile, and any Dockerfile.<name> beside it, in any case the tools read, and the Containerfile podman reads): the base image, the user it runs as, what it installs and from where. Before this, only review.yaml's deploy-config held the Dockerfile (#858, a gap #853's review named). dockerfile* and Containerfile* match no file yet (NOT_YET_FILES in test/merge-policy.test.ts).

The engine's deployment files at the top of its repo, beside deploy/**: a bare deploy path (a file, or a symlink to anywhere) and the compose files set how it runs, as the setup scripts do: the user, the mounts, the ports. Locked before the first one exists (NOT_YET_FILES in test/merge-policy.test.ts; #885).

The planners' decision records (#920): planner and plan-review agents read each one as a recorded decision, and a plan may cite it.
